scope: One existing, functional iOS app, one release/version, and submission to Apple App Store through the client's account.
Existing Swift or React Native iOS projects are considered after build review. The source must already build for iOS. Framework conversion and major SDK upgrades are separate.
Versioning, bundle identifier, signing and provisioning, and generation of the iOS release build using the client's Apple Developer account.
Up to three agreed core-flow checks on one physical iPhone plus a simulator where useful. No device compatibility matrix or full QA audit.
One English-language listing populated with client-supplied text, store-ready screenshots, icon, support/privacy URLs, age/content information, and reviewer credentials.
Technical assistance entering App Privacy answers based on the client's confirmed data practices and disclosed SDKs. Client confirms all business, legal and data-handling declarations.
Upload the build and submit one release for store review. Provide submission confirmation, version/build details, configuration changes, and handoff instructions.

Seven-day delivery refers to initial submission after all account, asset and app prerequisites are ready. Apple's processing, review, approval and publication timing are outside the service provider's control.

One revision covers an in-scope metadata/signing correction and, if necessary, one resubmission requested within 30 days of initial submission. Product-code changes, entitlement-policy redesign, payment changes, rejection appeals, and further review rounds are separate.
Apple Developer account must belong to the client, be active/verified, and have necessary agreements completed. App Store Connect access and permissions must be ready for build upload and submission.

Client provides reviewer test access and required content, owns/has rights to the app, and pays account/provider fees. No tester recruitment, account lending, guaranteed acceptance, downloads, ranking, store artwork design, or legal-document writing.

requirements.text: Share your iOS repository, framework, working build instructions, bundle ID, and target version. Confirm the app already runs and builds for iOS. Identify any prior App Store rejection and include the review message.

Invite access to your active Apple Developer account and App Store Connect with the permissions needed to build, sign, upload, and submit. Confirm enrollment, verification, and required agreements are complete.

Provide final English listing text, icon, store-ready screenshots, support and privacy-policy URLs, category/age information, and availability settings. Confirm you have rights to the app and supplied materials.

Provide reviewer/demo credentials, up to 3 core flows to check, and details of data collection, third-party SDKs, login, payments, and account deletion. Confirm the existing app meets those requirements and provide approved disclosure answers.

Optional: share previous review messages, current store links, device-specific issues, or a preferred release date. Remove passwords and secrets from attachments. Review and publication dates cannot be guaranteed.

summary:
Get your existing iOS app prepared and submitted to the Apple App Store through your own developer account.

This package covers one iOS app and one release.

Included:
- Release versioning, signing, and build configuration
- A signed release build and checks of up to 3 core flows
- One English listing using your supplied text, icon, and screenshots
- Submission details and disclosures based on information you confirm
- Build upload and submission for review
- Configuration changes, submission confirmation, and handoff notes
- One metadata/signing revision and resubmission requested within 30 days

I built and released Agentic and SolPulse across web and mobile and have handled their release workflows.

Your iOS app must already work and build. Your developer account, assets, disclosures, and access must be ready. You pay account and service fees.

Delivery means submission within 7 days after prerequisites are ready. Apple controls approval and publication timing. App repairs, policy-driven feature changes, account appeals, and Android submission need separate scope.

Send your framework, app status, and account details before ordering.

faqs.q: Does this include Android or Google Play?
faqs.a: This listing covers one iOS app release submitted to Apple App Store. Google Play submission requires a separate scope. You must provide a working iOS project; converting a web or Android app to iOS is a separate service.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee approval or a publication date?
faqs.a: No. The deliverable is a prepared iOS build and submitted release. Apple controls approval and publication timing. The 7-day delivery starts after the app, assets, account permissions, and required agreements are ready.

faqs.q: Do I need my own Apple Developer account?
faqs.a: Yes. You need active Apple Developer membership and must invite the necessary App Store Connect and signing access. You pay Apple's fees and complete enrollment and agreements. I submit through your account, not an account I own.

faqs.q: What happens if the store rejects the app?
faqs.a: One metadata/signing correction and resubmission requested within 30 days is included. App-code changes, payment or privacy feature changes, account appeals, and additional review rounds need separate scope. Store acceptance is not guaranteed.

faqs.q: What must I supply, and whose account is used?
faqs.a: Your active developer account, app source, listing text, icon, screenshots, support/privacy URLs, and reviewer access. You confirm disclosures and pay fees. I use invited access to your account. Store artwork and legal-document writing are separate.
